sanskrit: raṇe vinihataṃ śrutvā śokārtā vai vinaṃkṣyati subhadrā vakṣyate kiṃ mām abhimanyum apaśyatī draupadī caiva duḥkhārte te ca vakṣyāmi kiṃ nv aham
english: When she hears that he has been slain in battle, Subhadrā, stricken with grief, will surely perish. Not seeing Abhimanyu, what will she say to me? And Draupadī too, anguished with sorrow—what shall I say to them both?

sanskrit: vajrasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ yan na yāsyati sahasradhā vadhūṃ dṛṣṭvā rudatīṃ śokakarśitām
english: Surely my heart is made of the hardness of the thunderbolt, that it does not shatter into a thousand pieces when I behold the young bride weeping, wasted away with grief.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭānāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ siṃhanādo mayā śrutaḥ yuyutsuś cāpi kṛṣṇena śruto vīrān upālabhan
english: I heard the lion's roar of the exultant sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Yuyutsu too was heard by Kṛṣṇa, reproaching their warriors.

sanskrit: aśaknuvanto bībhatsuṃ bālaṃ hatvā mahārathāḥ kiṃ nadadhvam adharmajñāḥ pārthe vai dṛśyatāṃ balam
english: "Unable to face Bībhatsu, you great chariot-warriors who slew a mere boy—why do you roar, you who know nothing of dharma? Let your strength be shown against Pārtha himself!"

sanskrit: kiṃ tayor vipriyaṃ kṛtvā keśavārjunayor mṛdhe siṃhavan nadata prītāḥ śokakāla upasthite
english: "Having wrought this outrage against Keśava and Arjuna in battle, why do you roar like lions in delight, when an hour of grief is upon you?"

sanskrit: āgamiṣyati vaḥ kṣipraṃ phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ adharmo hi kṛtas tīvraḥ kathaṃ syād aphalaś ciram
english: "Swiftly the fruit of your evil deed will come upon you. A grievous unrighteousness has been done—how should it stay fruitless for long?"

sanskrit: iti tān prati bhāṣan vai vaiśyāputro mahāmatiḥ apāyāc chastram utsṛjya kopaduḥkhasamanvitaḥ
english: Thus speaking against them, the high-minded son of the vaiśya woman cast aside his weapon and departed, filled with wrath and sorrow.

sanskrit: kimartham etann ākhyātaṃ tvayā kṛṣṇa raṇe mama adhakṣyaṃ tān ahaṃ sarvāṃs tadā krūrān mahārathān
english: "Why, Kṛṣṇa, was this told to me in the field? Else I would have burned them all then—those cruel great chariot-warriors."

sanskrit: nigṛhya vāsudevas taṃ putrādhibhir abhiplutam maivam ity abravīt kṛṣṇas tīvraśokasamanvitam
english: Restraining him as he was overwhelmed by anguish for his son, Vāsudeva—Kṛṣṇa—said "Not so!" to him who was filled with bitter grief.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eṣa vai panthāḥ śūrāṇām anivartinām kṣatriyāṇāṃ viśeṣeṇa yeṣāṃ yuddhena jīvikā
english: "This is the path of all heroes who never turn back—above all of kṣatriyas, whose livelihood is war."

sanskrit: eṣā vai yudhyamānānāṃ śūrāṇām anivartinām vihitā dharmaśāstrajñair gatir gatimatāṃ vara
english: "This is the destiny ordained by those who know the law for heroes who fight and never retreat, O best of those who attain their goal."

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ yuddhe hi maraṇaṃ śūrāṇām anivartinām gataḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ lokān abhimanyur na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Death in battle is certain for heroes who never turn back. Abhimanyu has gone to the worlds of those who have done meritorious deeds—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: etac ca sarvavīrāṇāṃ kāṅkṣitaṃ bharatarṣabha saṃgrāme 'bhimukhā mṛtyuṃ prapnuyāmeti mānada
english: "And this is the very wish of all heroes, O bull of the Bhāratas: 'May we meet death face to face in battle,' O giver of honor."

sanskrit: sa ca vīrān raṇe hatvā rājaputrān mahābalān vīrair ākāṅkṣitaṃ mṛtyuṃ saṃprāpto 'bhimukho raṇe
english: "And he, having slain mighty heroes and princes in the field, has attained the death longed for by heroes, fronting it in battle."

sanskrit: mā śucaḥ puruṣavyāghra pūrvair eṣa sanātanaḥ dharmakṛdbhiḥ kṛto dharmaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ raṇe kṣayaḥ
english: "Grieve not, O tiger among men. This is the eternal law made by the righteous men of old: that the kṣatriyas should perish in battle."

sanskrit: ime te bhrātaraḥ sarve dīnā bharatasattama tvayi śokasamāviṣṭe nṛpāś ca suhṛdas tava
english: "All these your brothers are downcast, O best of the Bhāratas, while you are overwhelmed by grief—and so are the kings, your friends."

sanskrit: etāṃs tvaṃ vacasā sāmnā samāśvāsaya mānada viditaṃ veditavyaṃ te na śokaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "Comfort them with gentle words, O giver of honor. You know what is to be known; you ought not to give way to grief."

sanskrit: evam āśvāsitaḥ pārthaḥ kṛṣṇenādbhutakarmaṇā tato 'bravīt tadā bhrātṝn sarvān pārthaḥ sagadgadān
english: Thus consoled by Kṛṣṇa of wondrous deeds, Pārtha then spoke to all his brothers, who were choked with sobs.

sanskrit: sa dīrghabāhuḥ pṛthvaṃso dīrgharājīvalocanaḥ abhimanyur yathā vṛttaḥ śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ tathā
english: That long-armed, broad-shouldered one, with eyes like long lotus-petals, said: "How Abhimanyu fell—just so I wish to hear it."

sanskrit: sanāgasyandanahayān drakṣyadhvaṃ nihatān mayā saṃgrāme sānubandhāṃs tān mama putrasya vairiṇaḥ
english: "You shall behold my son's foes slain by me in battle, together with their elephants, chariots, and horses, and all their kinsmen."

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca vaḥ kṛtāstrāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ śastrapāṇinām saubhadro nidhanaṃ gacched vajriṇāpi samāgataḥ
english: "How, with all of you accomplished in arms and weapons in hand, could the son of Subhadrā meet his death—he who could withstand even the wielder of the thunderbolt?"

sanskrit: yady evam aham ajñāsyam aśaktān rakṣaṇe mama putrasya pāṇḍupāñcālān mayā gupto bhavet tataḥ
english: "Had I known that the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas were thus unable to protect my son, he would have been guarded by me."

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca vo rathasthānāṃ śaravarṣāṇi muñcatām nīto 'bhimanyur nidhanaṃ kadarthīkṛtya vaḥ paraiḥ
english: "And how, while you stood in your chariots loosing showers of arrows, was Abhimanyu brought to his death, you being set at naught by the foe?"

sanskrit: aho vaḥ pauruṣaṃ nāsti na ca vo 'sti parākramaḥ yatrābhimanyuḥ samare paśyatāṃ vo nipātitaḥ
english: "Alas, there is no manhood in you, nor any valor, since Abhimanyu was struck down in the battle before your very eyes."

sanskrit: ātmānam eva garheyaṃ yad ahaṃ vaḥ sudurbalān yuṣmān ājñāya niryāto bhīrūn akṛtaniśramān
english: "Nay, I should blame myself, that knowing you so feeble, so timid and untrained in toil, I yet went forth and left you."

sanskrit: āho svid bhūṣaṇārthāya varmaśastrāyudhāni vaḥ vācaś ca vaktuṃ saṃsatsu mama putram arakṣatām
english: "Or were your armor, weapons, and arms worn only for ornament, and your speeches only to be uttered in assemblies—since you did not guard my son?"

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato vākyaṃ tiṣṭhaṃś cāpavarāsimān na smāśakyata bībhatsuḥ kena cit prasamīkṣitum
english: Having spoken these words, Bībhatsu stood there, the bearer of the bow and sword, and no one could bear to look upon him.

sanskrit: tam antakam iva kruddhaṃ niḥśvasantaṃ muhur muhuḥ putraśokābhisaṃtaptam aśrupūrṇamukhaṃ tadā
english: He was like Death enraged, sighing again and again, scorched by grief for his son, his face filled with tears.

sanskrit: nābhibhāṣṭuṃ śaknuvanti draṣṭuṃ vā suhṛdo 'rjunam anyatra vāsudevād vā jyeṣṭād vā pāṇḍunandanāt
english: His friends could neither speak to Arjuna nor even look upon him—none save Vāsudeva and the eldest son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: sarvāsv avasthāsu hitāv arjunasya manonugau bahumānāt priyatvāc ca tāv enaṃ vaktum arhataḥ
english: Those two, devoted to Arjuna's welfare in all conditions and dear to his heart—they alone, through his high regard and love, were fit to address him.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ putraśokena bhṛśaṃ pīḍitamānasam rājīvalocanaṃ kruddhaṃ rājā vacanam abravīt
english: Then to him, his mind sorely tormented by grief for his son, the lotus-eyed one in his wrath, the king spoke these words.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tvayi yāte mahābāho saṃśaptakabalaṃ prati prayatnam akarot tīvram ācāryo grahaṇe mama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When you had gone, O mighty-armed one, against the host of the Saṃśaptakas, the teacher made a fierce effort to take me captive.

sanskrit: vyāḍhānīkaṃ vayaṃ droṇaṃ varayāmaḥ sma sarvaśaḥ prativyūhya rathānīkaṃ yatamānaṃ tathā raṇe
english: We held Droṇa back on every side as he marshaled his battle-array, arraying our own host of chariots against him as he strove in the fight.

sanskrit: sa vāryamāṇo rathibhī rakṣitena mayā tathā asmān api jaghānāśu pīḍayan niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Though held off by the chariot-warriors who guarded me, he swiftly smote even us, harrying us with his whetted shafts.

sanskrit: te pīḍyamānā droṇena droṇānīkaṃ na śaknumaḥ prativīkṣitum apy ājau bhettuṃ tat kuta eva tu
english: So hard pressed by Droṇa, we could not even gaze upon Droṇa's array in the battle—how then could we break it?

sanskrit: vayaṃ tv apratimaṃ vīrye sarve saubhadram ātmajam uktavantaḥ sma te tāta bhindhy anīkam iti prabho
english: Then all of us said to your son, the son of Subhadrā, peerless in valor: "Dear child, break the array, O lord!"

sanskrit: sa tathā codito 'smābhiḥ sadaśva iva vīryavān asahyam api taṃ bhāraṃ voḍhum evopacakrame
english: Thus urged by us, that valorous one, like a noble steed, set himself to bear even that unbearable burden.

sanskrit: sa tavāstropadeśena vīryeṇa ca samanvitaḥ prāviśat tad balaṃ bālaḥ suparṇa iva sāgaram
english: Endowed with your instruction in arms and with his own prowess, the boy entered that host as Suparṇa plunges into the sea.

sanskrit: te 'nuyātā vayaṃ vīraṃ sātvatīputram āhave praveṣṭukāmās tenaiva yena sa prāviśac camūm
english: We followed that hero, the son of the Sātvata princess, into the fray, eager to enter by the very breach through which he had pierced the host.

sanskrit: tataḥ saindhavako rājā kṣudras tāta jayadrathaḥ varadānena rudrasya sarvān naḥ samavārayat
english: Then the king of the Sindhus, the base Jayadratha, dear child, by a boon granted of Rudra held us all back.

sanskrit: tato droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ karṇo drauṇiś ca sa bṛhadbalaḥ kṛtavarmā ca saubhadraṃ ṣaḍ rathāḥ paryavārayan
english: Then Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, the son of Droṇa, Bṛhadbala, and Kṛtavarman—six chariot-warriors—surrounded the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: parivārya tu taiḥ sarvair yudhi bālo mahārathaiḥ yatamānaḥ paraṃ śaktyā bahubhir virathīkṛtaḥ
english: Hemmed in by all those great chariot-warriors, the boy, striving to the utmost of his strength, was deprived of his chariot by their many hands.

sanskrit: tato dauḥśāsaniḥ kṣipraṃ tathā tair virathīkṛtam saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ prāpya diṣṭāntenābhyayojayat
english: Then the son of Duḥśāsana, when he had thus been swiftly stripped of his chariot and brought to utter peril, dispatched him to his appointed end.

sanskrit: sa tu hatvā sahasrāṇi dvipāśvarathasādinām rājaputraśataṃ cāgryaṃ vīrāṃś cālakṣitān bahūn
english: But he had slain thousands of riders on elephants, horses, and chariots, a full hundred foremost princes, and many unnamed heroes,

sanskrit: bṛhadbalaṃ ca rājānaṃ svargeṇājau prayojya ha tataḥ paramadharmātmā diṣṭāntam upajagmivān
english: and having sent King Bṛhadbala to heaven in the fight—then that one of supremely righteous soul met his appointed end.

sanskrit: etāvad eva nirvṛttam asmākaṃ śokavardhanam sa caivaṃ puruṣavyāghraḥ svargalokam avāptavān
english: This is all that has befallen us, swelling our grief; and so that tiger among men has attained the world of heaven.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato 'rjuno vacaḥ śrutvā dharmarājena bhāṣitam hā putra iti niḥśvasya vyathito nyapatad bhuvi
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Arjuna, hearing the words spoken by the Dharma-king, sighed "Alas, my son!" and, stricken, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: viṣaṇṇavadanāḥ sarve parigṛhya dhanaṃjayam netrair animiṣair dīnāḥ pratyavekṣan parasparam
english: With downcast faces all of them clasped Dhanaṃjaya, and, wretched, gazed upon one another with unblinking eyes.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ vāsaviḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ kampamāno jvareṇeva niḥśvasaṃś ca muhur muhuḥ
english: Then the son of Vāsava, regaining his senses, swooning with rage, trembling as if in a fever and sighing again and again,

sanskrit: pāṇiṃ pāṇau viniṣpiṣya śvasamāno 'śrunetravān unmatta iva viprekṣann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: wringing hand in hand, breathing hard, his eyes streaming with tears, glaring about him like a madman, spoke these words:

sanskrit: satyaṃ vaḥ pratijānāmi śvo 'smi hantā jayadratham na ced vadhabhayād bhīto dhārtarāṣṭrān prahāsyati
english: "Truly I vow to you: tomorrow I shall be the slayer of Jayadratha—unless, frightened by fear of death, he abandons the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra,

sanskrit: na cāsmāñ śaraṇaṃ gacchet kṛṣṇaṃ vā puruṣottamam bhavantaṃ vā mahārāja śvo 'smi hantā jayadratham
english: and unless he seeks refuge with us, or with Kṛṣṇa the supreme being, or with you, O great king—tomorrow I shall be the slayer of Jayadratha!

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrapriyakaraṃ mayi vismṛtasauhṛdam pāpaṃ bālavadhe hetuṃ śvo 'smi hantā jayadratham
english: That doer of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's pleasure, who has forgotten his friendship toward me, the wicked one who was the cause of the boy's death—tomorrow I shall be the slayer of Jayadratha!

sanskrit: rakṣamāṇāś ca taṃ saṃkhye ye māṃ yotsyanti ke cana api droṇakṛpau vīrau chādayiṣyāmi tāñ śaraiḥ
english: And whoever shall fight against me while guarding him in the battle—even the heroes Droṇa and Kṛpa—those I shall cover over with my arrows.

sanskrit: yady etad evaṃ saṃgrāme na kuryāṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ mā sma puṇyakṛtāṃ lokān prāpnuyāṃ śūrasaṃmatān
english: "If I do not accomplish this thus in the battle, O bulls among men, may I not attain the worlds of the righteous, honored by heroes—

sanskrit: ye lokā mātṛhantṝṇāṃ ye cāpi pitṛghātinām gurudāragāmināṃ ye ca piśunānāṃ ca ye tathā
english: those worlds that are for slayers of mothers, for killers of fathers, for those who violate the teacher's wife, and for slanderers,

sanskrit: sādhūn asūyatāṃ ye ca ye cāpi parivādinām ye ca nikṣepahartṝṇāṃ ye ca viśvāsaghātinām
english: and for those who revile the good, and for backbiters, and for those who steal what is left in trust, and for betrayers of confidence;

sanskrit: bhuktapūrvāṃ striyaṃ ye ca nindatām aghaśaṃsinām brahmaghnānāṃ ca ye lokā ye ca goghātinām api
english: the worlds of those who revile a woman they have once enjoyed, of speakers of evil, of slayers of brahmins, and of killers of cattle as well;

sanskrit: pāyasaṃ vā yavānnaṃ vā śākaṃ kṛsaram eva vā saṃyāvāpūpamāṃsāni ye ca lokā vṛthāśnatām tān ahnaivādhigaccheyaṃ na ced dhanyāṃ jayadratham
english: the worlds of those who eat in vain milk-pudding or barley-food, vegetables, or rice-and-sesame, wheat-cakes, baked sweets, or meat—into those very worlds may I go this day, if I do not slay Jayadratha.

sanskrit: vedādhyāyinam atyarthaṃ saṃśitaṃ vā dvijottamam avamanyamāno yān yāti vṛddhān sādhūṃs tathā gurūn
english: "Those worlds to which a man goes who scorns a diligent student of the Veda, a steadfast and best of brahmins, the aged, the good, and his teachers—

sanskrit: spṛśatāṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gāṃ ca pādenāgniṃ ca yāṃ labhet yāpsu śleṣma purīṣaṃ vā mūtraṃ vā muñcatāṃ gatiḥ tāṃ gaccheyaṃ gatiṃ ghorāṃ na ced dhanyāṃ jayadratham
english: the destiny one earns by touching a brahmin, a cow, or the fire with one's foot, the destiny of those who cast phlegm, ordure, or urine into the waters—to that dreadful destiny may I go, if I do not slay Jayadratha.

sanskrit: nagnasya snāyamānasya yā ca vandhyātither gatiḥ utkocināṃ mṛṣoktīnāṃ vañcakānāṃ ca yā gatiḥ ātmāpahāriṇāṃ yā ca yā ca mithyābhiśaṃsinām
english: "The destiny of one who bathes naked, of one whose guest departs unfed, the destiny of takers of bribes, of liars, and of deceivers, the destiny of those who give themselves false airs and of those who bear false witness—

sanskrit: bhṛtyaiḥ saṃdṛśyamānānāṃ putradārāśritais tathā asaṃvibhajya kṣudrāṇāṃ yā gatir mṛṣṭam aśnatām tāṃ gaccheyaṃ gatiṃ ghorāṃ na ced dhanyāṃ jayadratham
english: the destiny of the mean who, watched by their servants and dependents, their sons and wives, eat dainty food without sharing—to that dreadful destiny may I go, if I do not slay Jayadratha.

sanskrit: saṃśritaṃ vāpi yas tyaktvā sādhuṃ tadvacane ratam na bibharti nṛśaṃsātmā nindate copakāriṇam
english: "He who, cruel of soul, forsakes a good man who has taken refuge with him and is devoted to his word, fails to support him, and reviles his benefactor;

sanskrit: arhate prātiveśyāya śrāddhaṃ yo na dadāti ca anarhate ca yo dadyād vṛṣalīpatyur eva ca
english: he who gives no funeral offering to a worthy neighbor, and gives it instead to the unworthy, and the husband of a śūdra woman—

sanskrit: madyapo bhinnamaryādaḥ kṛtaghno bhrātṛnindakaḥ teṣāṃ gatim iyāṃ kṣipraṃ na ced dhanyāṃ jayadratham
english: the drunkard, the breaker of bounds, the ingrate, the reviler of his brother—their destiny may I swiftly come to, if I do not slay Jayadratha.

sanskrit: dharmād apetā ye cānye mayā nātrānukīrtitāḥ ye cānukīrtitāḥ kṣipraṃ teṣāṃ gatim avāpnuyām yadi vyuṣṭām imāṃ rātriṃ śvo na hanyāṃ jayadratham
english: "And the others fallen from dharma whom I have not named here, and those whom I have named—may I swiftly attain their destiny, if, when this night has passed, I do not slay Jayadratha tomorrow.

sanskrit: imāṃ cāpy aparāṃ bhūyaḥ pratijñāṃ me nibodhata yady asminn ahate pāpe sūryo 'stam upayāsyati ihaiva saṃpraveṣṭāhaṃ jvalitaṃ jātavedasam
english: "And hear this further vow of mine besides: if the sun should go down while this wicked one is yet unslain, here on this very spot I shall enter the blazing fire.

sanskrit: asurasuramanuṣyāḥ pakṣiṇo voragā vā; pitṛrajanicarā vā brahmadevarṣayo vā caram acaram apīdaṃ yat paraṃ cāpi tasmāt; tad api mama ripuṃ taṃ rakṣituṃ naiva śaktāḥ
english: "Asuras, gods, or men, birds or serpents, the fathers or the night-roamers, the brahmā-seers or the divine seers, all that moves and all that moves not, and whatever is beyond even that—none of these is able to guard that foe of mine from me.

sanskrit: yadi viśati rasātalaṃ tadagryaṃ; viyad api devapuraṃ diteḥ puraṃ vā tad api śaraśatair ahaṃ prabhāte; bhṛśam abhipatya ripoḥ śiro 'bhihartā
english: "Though he enter the uttermost depths of the netherworld, or the sky, or the city of the gods, or the city of Diti—even there, at daybreak, with hundreds of arrows, falling fiercely upon him, I shall strike off my foe's head."

sanskrit: evam uktvā vicikṣepa gāṇḍīvaṃ savyadakṣiṇam tasya śabdam atikramya dhanuḥśabdo 'spṛśad divam
english: Having spoken thus, he drew the Gāṇḍīva to left and right; and surpassing his very voice, the twang of the bow touched the heavens.

sanskrit: arjunena pratijñāte pāñcajanyaṃ janārdanaḥ pradadhmau tatra saṃkruddho devadattaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: When Arjuna had taken his vow, Janārdana, sorely wrathful, blew his conch Pāñcajanya, and Dhanaṃjaya his Devadatta.

sanskrit: sa pāñcajanyo 'cyutavaktravāyunā; bhṛśaṃ supūrṇodaraniḥsṛtadhvaniḥ jagat sapātālaviyaddigīśvaraṃ; prakampayām āsa yugātyaye yathā
english: That Pāñcajanya, its sound bursting forth from its well-filled belly through the breath of Acyuta's mouth, set the whole world trembling—with its netherworlds, its sky, and the guardians of the quarters—as at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: tato vāditraghoṣāś ca prādurāsan samantataḥ siṃhanādāś ca pāṇḍūnāṃ pratijñāte mahātmanā
english: Then the sounds of instruments arose on every side, and the lion-roars of the Pāṇḍavas, when the great-souled one had taken his vow.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śrutvā tu taṃ mahāśabdaṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ putragṛddhinām cāraiḥ pravedite tatra samutthāya jayadrathaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: But hearing that mighty uproar of the Pāṇḍavas who were grieving for the boy, and informed of it there by his spies, Jayadratha rose up,

sanskrit: śokasaṃmūḍhahṛdayo duḥkhenābhihato bhṛśam majjamāna ivāgādhe vipule śokasāgare
english: his heart bewildered with grief, sorely smitten by sorrow, like one sinking in a fathomless, vast ocean of woe.

sanskrit: jagāma samitiṃ rājñāṃ saindhavo vimṛśan bahu sa teṣāṃ naradevānāṃ sakāśe paridevayan
english: The lord of the Sindhus went, pondering much, to the assembly of the kings, and there in the presence of those god-like rulers he made his lament.

sanskrit: abhimanyoḥ pitur bhītaḥ savrīḍo vākyam abravīt yo 'sau pāṇḍoḥ kila kṣetre jātaḥ śakreṇa kāminā
english: Fearful of Abhimanyu's father, abashed, he spoke these words: "That one who was begotten, they say, in Pāṇḍu's field by Śakra in his desire—

sanskrit: sa ninīṣati durbuddhir māṃ kilaikaṃ yamakṣayam tat svasti vo 'stu yāsyāmi svagṛhaṃ jīvitepsayā
english: "that evil-minded one means, they say, to lead me alone to the abode of Yama. Therefore, fare you well—I shall go to my own home, in my longing to live.

sanskrit: atha vā stha pratibalās trātuṃ māṃ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ pārthena prārthitaṃ vīrās te dadantu mamābhayam
english: "Or, if you are strong enough to save me, O bulls among kṣatriyas, then, heroes, grant me—whom Pārtha has marked for death—your protection."
